method.deseasonalization: Iterative multiplicative seasonal adjustment (5 passes): 2x12 centered MA trend -> median month-of-year ratio -> factors normalized to mean 1.0 -> series / factors. Estimated per (kind x window) independently.
method.window_correction: 24hr counts are divided by a trailing 12-month median share of the final total, restating them as final-total-equivalents so the 24hr and 21d indexes share a common scale and the 24hr index can nowcast a thread on its first day.
method.rebasing: Each deseasonalized series is rebased to 100 = mean over the common overlap period 2014-07 onward.

indexes.badness_index: HEADLINE. 100 * wants_index / hiring_index, i.e. seasonally adjusted job-seeker volume relative to employer-post volume. 100 = average badness over 2014-07..latest; 200 = twice as bad as average, 50 = half as bad. Higher = worse for job seekers. Scale-free: HN audience growth cancels out.
indexes.badness_percentile: Empirical percentile of this month's badness within the whole index period (100 = worst month on record).
indexes.badness_band: good for seekers (<50), better than average (50-100), worse than average (100-200), bad (200-300), very bad (>=300).
indexes.hiring_index: Deseasonalized employer-post volume (demand). Its level is partly contaminated by HN audience growth.
indexes.wants_index: Deseasonalized job-seeker volume (supply). Its level is partly contaminated by HN audience growth.
indexes.tightness_index: Deprecated alias of badness_index, kept for backward compatibility. Note it is the inverse of the economist's usual 'tightness' (vacancies per unemployed).
indexes.activity_index: sqrt(hiring_index * wants_index). Overall job-thread engagement; NOT scale-free, so it partly tracks HN's own traffic.

method.window_choice: 21d captures 99.9-100% of final comments with no next-month overlap (r=1.000 with total) and is the recommended basis. 24hr is the fast nowcast (r=0.976 with total).
method.excluded: Months with no complete 21d window are excluded (see partial_months).

facts.definition: Badness = 100 x (seasonally adjusted 'who wants to be hired' volume) / (seasonally adjusted 'who is hiring' volume). 100 = average over the index period; higher = worse for job seekers.
reading_examples: Best month on record: 2018-05 at 15.86 (64 seeker vs 1177 hiring comments in 21d).
Latest month: 2026-10 at 504.32 (692 seeker vs 388 hiring comments in 21d) — 31.8x the best month.
100 means exactly as bad as the 2014-2026 average; 200 means twice as bad; 50 means half as bad.

seasonality_removed.note: Max month-of-year deviation from a centered 2x12 MA, in percent. Lower = less residual seasonality. Raw uses all mature months; adjusted uses the index overlap period.

window_disagreement_notes: Largest 21d-vs-24hr gaps occur in low-volume months where the 24hr count is a small denominator (e.g. 2016-01 wants had 31 comments in its first 24h) and in slow-start months (2024-09 hiring captured only 44% of its total in 24h vs 66% in August).
These are window-measurement artifacts, not data errors: the 21d window is unaffected because it captures ~100% of final comments.

partial_months.note: Posted 338.7h ago; even the 24hr window is incomplete, so this month is excluded from the index. The 24hr index becomes available 24h after posting, the 21d index after 21 days.
